perf.summary: Replace per-cell multiply (y*width+x) with a running counter; the value being stored equals the linear index itself.
perf.currentCost: Each inner iteration computes y*width+x (1 IMUL + 1 ADD) plus index++ (separate counter). The stored value y*width+x is, by construction, identical to the running index that walks the buffer.
perf.proposedChange: Drop the nested loops and the multiply entirely: int total = width * height; for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) ptr[i] = i; Since cells are written in row-major order, ptr[index] always receives the value 'index'. This is a single tight loop Burst vectorizes trivially (store of an incrementing vector).
perf.rationale: Eliminates one IMUL per cell and the outer-loop bookkeeping, collapsing two nested loops into one linear pass with a self-incrementing store value. Lower dependency chain and SIMD-friendly (broadcast iota).
perf.risk: Semantics-preserving only because the write order is row-major and value == linear index. width*height must not overflow int (already implied: index is int and ptr[index++] uses the same range, so no new overflow risntroduced). Empty grid (total==0) handled by loop guard.
